name: r_p_0
description: Baseline periosteal radius of the humeral diaphysis (inferred from the order of magnitude of total area). Site-specific absolute values await full-text confirmation.

name: r_e_0
description: Baseline endocortical radius of the humeral diaphysis (inferred from the order of magnitude of medullary cavity area). Awaits full-text confirmation.

name: E_ref
description: Reference elastic modulus of cortical bone matrix (at f_bm = 1 and baseline mineralisation).

name: kappa_E
description: Exponent of E_app on f_bm, CORTICAL compartment. Adopted from Currey 1988 at v2.17 (P5m): log E = -4.84 + 2.55 log(calcium) + 3.13 log(V_f), R^2 = 0.83, on compact bone from 18 species. P5l had tried this value GLOBALLY and had to revert it, because Currey measured compact bone and the exponent cannot be extrapolated to the trabecular compartment; P5m instead lets trabecularParams override it to 2.0, the Gibson-Ashby open-cell scaling appropriate to a cellular solid. The former compromise of 2.5 was, on this reading, correct for neither compartment. The closed-loop identity d ln eps/d ln f_bm = -kappa_E now reads -3.13 in cortex and -2.00 in the vertebra.

name: nu_E
description: Exponent of E_app on mineralisation. ADOPTED FROM THE SOURCE AT v2.16 (P5l): Currey 1988's two-variable fit, log E = -4.84 + 2.55 log(calcium) + 3.13 log(V_f) at R^2 = 0.83, gives 2.55 on calcium content against the 1.0 previously assumed, and the former upper bound of 2.0 excluded it. Unlike the volume-fraction exponent, this one transfers safely: mineral density sits at its baseline in both compartments, so raising it does not disturb the trabecular modulus (verified: trabecular E_app unaffected, no drift, elastic domain intact).

name: f_bm_min
description: Numerical floor. Since E_app is proportional to f_bm^kappa, strain diverges as f_bm approaches zero.

name: eps_elastic_max
description: Yield strain of cortical bone, ~7000 microstrain (Bayraktar 2004; Morgan & Keaveny). NOT a model parameter but a validity boundary: the model assumes linear elasticity E_app = E_ref*f_bm^kappa_E throughout, and beyond yield that assumption fails, the tissue entering damage or fracture rather than adaptation. simulate() flags this as out.validity.ok; simulations at pathologically low f_bm trigger it. The highest strain in any normal scenario is the tennis-loading case at 2851 microstrain, well below this bound.

name: f_bm_0
description: Baseline bone matrix volume fraction of cortical bone (cortical porosity ~5%).

name: rho_min_0
description: Baseline mean tissue mineral density (ash-density scale).

name: M_L_0
description: Baseline peak bending moment of daily activity (humeral diaphysis). scenarioLibrary uses this as the 1.0x reference.

name: F_L_0
description: Baseline peak axial force of daily activity.

name: k_perm
description: Intrinsic permeability of the lacunocanalicular network. WEINBAUM 1994 READ AT v2.20 (Reference/a05.pdf). It does NOT yield this parameter directly: the paper computes shear on the osteocyte process from a fibre-matrix theory rather than exposing a lumped amplification we could read off, so K_tau cannot yet be derived from it. What it does give is a sharper check - see K_tau and tau_target_lo.

name: mu_fluid
description: Viscosity of bone interstitial fluid (close to water at 37 C).

name: S_stor
description: Poroelastic storage coefficient. WEINBAUM 1994 READ AT v2.20 (Reference/a05.pdf). It does NOT yield this parameter directly: the paper computes shear on the osteocyte process from a fibre-matrix theory rather than exposing a lumped amplification we could read off, so K_tau cannot yet be derived from it. What it does give is a sharper check - see K_tau and tau_target_lo.

name: a_canal
description: Canalicular radius. CONFIRMED AT v2.20 against Weinbaum 1994: the paper's geometry has an osteocyte process of radius a (order 0.1 micrometre) inside a canaliculus of radius b, and our 150 nm is consistent with that hierarchy. Weinbaum also fixes the GAG fibre spacing at Delta = 7 nm, validated against streaming-potential data, with 6-11 nm admissible - a length scale our lumped K_tau absorbs rather than represents.

name: Gamma_PCM
description: Pericellular matrix shear-stress amplification factor. WEINBAUM 1994 READ AT v2.20 (Reference/a05.pdf). It does NOT yield this parameter directly: the paper computes shear on the osteocyte process from a fibre-matrix theory rather than exposing a lumped amplification we could read off, so K_tau cannot yet be derived from it. What it does give is a sharper check - see K_tau and tau_target_lo.

name: L_poro
description: Poroelastic drainage path length (osteonal radius scale, canalicular network to Haversian canal). Together with c_p it sets the frequency corner.

name: K_tau
description: Lumped shear gain: peak shear stress tau_max per unit peak strain at f_0 = 1 Hz [Pa/strain]. Absorbs the three unknown microstructural parameters (a/2)*Gamma/S. STILL CALIBRATED, NOT DERIVED (v2.20): Weinbaum 1994 computes shear from a fibre-matrix theory and does not expose a lumped amplification to substitute here. But it does tighten the check. Weinbaum's own predicted shear stresses are 10-20 dyn/cm^2, i.e. 1-2 Pa, which he notes coincides with where an adaptive remodelling response is seen - NARROWER than the 0.8-3.0 Pa band we calibrate against. Our baseline sedentary shear is 1.57 Pa, inside that narrower window. K_tau is therefore better constrained than the 0.8-3.0 band implies, and confidence is raised from low to medium on that basis.

name: alpha_f
description: [Retired at v1.5] Exponent of the original phenomenological surrogate function. Superseded by the closed-form |k tanh(kL)|, so frequency dependence no longer carries an adjustable exponent. Retained for comparison only.

name: f_c
description: [Retired at v1.5] Original phenomenological corner frequency. The actual corner is set by t_poro = L^2/c_p and is not a free parameter.

name: f_0
description: Reference frequency of the surrogate function (a defining constant).

name: tau_target_lo
description: Lower bound of the physiological fluid-shear-stress range, used for validation (not a model parameter). Weinbaum 1994 predicts 10-20 dyn/cm^2 (1-2 Pa) and observes that this coincides with the range where adaptive remodelling is seen; our 0.8-3.0 Pa band is looser than that. Tightening it to 1-2 Pa would pin K_tau harder and remains an option - our baseline of 1.57 Pa would still pass.

name: tau_target_hi
description: Upper bound of the physiological fluid-shear-stress range, used for validation (not a model parameter).

name: tau_50
description: Half-activation shear stress of the mechanosensitive ion channel. Moved from M4 at v1.4. Awaits Li 2019 (Piezo1). A principal source of divergence in the bifurcation analysis (E6).

name: k_tau_sig
description: Steepness of the channel-activation sigmoid. Moved from M4 at v1.4, and now carries the supralinear role of the former phenomenological exponent q. Reduced from 0.30 to 0.12 at v1.5: at 0.30, k_co(0) reaches 3.4% of k_co_max and the resting open probability is 4.6%, so loading raises the daily dose by only 5.6% (the signal is swamped by baseline) and the disuse loss target V2 cannot be met. A value of 0.12 gives a sedentary-to-bedrest dose ratio of 8.4, which is reasonable. Still a placeholder: Fu 2025 arrived at v2.18 but carries the equations, not the values (see k_co_max).

name: k_co_max
description: Maximum closed-to-open rate. Awaits the rate constants themselves. STATUS AT v2.18: Fu 2025 is now in hand (Reference/a01.pdf) and does NOT unlock this. Fu's main text gives the three-state ODEs but with SIX rates k1-k6, two of them functions of shear, which is not a one-to-one match to our four; and the numerical values live in an Appendix that the interlibrary scan does not include. What is still needed is Fu's supplementary material, or its source for the kinetics, Mao F, Yang Y, Jiang H, Biophys J 2022;121:4740-4747 - a finger-tactile electromechanical model, not a bone study, from which Fu borrowed the channel kinetics.

description: Open-to-closed rate. Awaits the rate constants themselves. STATUS AT v2.18: Fu 2025 is now in hand (Reference/a01.pdf) and does NOT unlock this. name: k_ic
description: Inactivated-to-closed recovery rate. Governs the rest-insertion gain (V5); recovery time approximately 10 s. Awaits the rate constants themselves. name: T_day
description: Seconds per day. Used to non-dimensionalise D_mech into a daily mean open probability.

name: J_max
description: Maximum Ca2+ influx rate (non-dimensionalised so that the baseline steady state is 1).

name: J_alt
description: Lumped term for parallel pathways (integrin, primary cilium, connexin 43). Its uncertainty is covered by the E6 sensitivity analysis.

name: k_C
description: Intracellular Ca2+ clearance rate (timescale of minutes).

name: k_Y
description: YAP/TAZ nuclear translocation rate.

name: K_Y
description: Half-saturation Ca2+ concentration for YAP/TAZ activation (dimensionless).

name: n_Y
description: Hill coefficient for YAP/TAZ activation.

name: delta_Y
description: YAP/TAZ deactivation rate.

name: beta_S
description: Basal sclerostin secretion rate. One of the divergence parameters in the bifurcation analysis (E6).

name: K_S
description: Half-saturation constant for YAP/TAZ inhibition of SOST. RECALIBRATED AT v2.14 (P5k) from 1.27: with bone calcium flux now real, unloading suppresses PTH, which damps resorption and slows disuse loss, so a more sensitive mechanical SOST response is needed to hold V2. Sets V2 = 1.196 %/month. V2 remains extremely sensitive to this parameter (1.10 gives 1.91 %/month, 1.24 gives 0.91), a steep transition near the set point and a key E6 finding.

name: h_S
description: Hill coefficient for mechanical inhibition of SOST.

name: delta_S
description: Sclerostin clearance rate.

name: delta_ab
description: Additional sclerostin clearance induced by the anti-sclerostin antibody (romosozumab). Calibrated at v2.14 (P5k); sets V8 to +12.16 % in the trabecular compartment. Briefly retuned to 1.65 during P5l and restored when the kappa_E change was reverted. Acts only while dosing, so V1, V2, V7 and the V6/V14 hold-outs are untouched by it.

name: sost_reb
description: Plateau of the compensatory up-regulation of SOST transcription under sustained antibody exposure. A = 0 at baseline and in every untreated scenario, so V1, V2, V7, V6 and V14 are structurally unaffected. RECALIBRATED AT v2.14 (P5k), where it also lost most of its leverage on V16: raising it 33 % moves V16 by 0.019, because the rebuilt calcium coupling damps the resorption overshoot faster than the rebound can drive it. The calibration target remains V16, not V10, which is why V10 stays a hold-out prediction.

name: tau_reb
description: Relaxation time constant of the compensatory SOST up-regulation (added at v2.10). Set from the clinical time course of rebound after romosozumab withdrawal: CTX peaks about 3 months after the last dose and returns to baseline by about 12 months, corresponding to a time constant of roughly 120 days. The bounds span 1-12 months.

name: K_P_sost
description: Half-saturation constant for PTH inhibition of SOST. RECALIBRATED AT v2.14 (P5k) and now AT ITS UPPER BOUND, which is an interpretable limit rather than an arbitrary pin: large means PTH inhibition of SOST is weak, so the fit is asking for this pathway to be effectively absent - the same choice Lemaire and Pivonka make by omitting it. The arm opposes V7 (higher calcium lowers PTH, which would raise sclerostin), so switching it off is what lets V7 clear its band at all once serum calcium is properly regulated. Still correlated with lambda_P; see the identifiability analysis.

name: lambda_T
description: Maximum fold up-regulation of SOST by TNF-alpha. Risks compensating with lambda_E, so profile likelihood is required.

name: K_T
description: Half-saturation constant for the action of TNF-alpha.

name: k_T
description: TNF-alpha production rate under oestrogen deficiency.

name: K_E
description: Half-saturation constant for oestrogen inhibition of TNF-alpha (E2 non-dimensionalised, premenopausal = 1).

name: n_E
description: Hill coefficient for oestrogen inhibition of TNF-alpha.

name: delta_T_tnf
description: TNF-alpha clearance rate.

name: n_ot_0
description: Baseline osteocyte density (defined as 1 by non-dimensionalisation).

name: n_ot_max
description: Upper bound on osteocyte density.

name: k_ot
description: Rate of osteocyte burial during bone formation.

name: gamma_ot
description: Proportionality coefficient for osteocyte removal by bone resorption.

name: delta_ot_0
description: Basal osteocyte apoptosis rate (rises with falling oestrogen and with age).

name: zeta
description: Exponent of the mechanosensing gain (n_ot/n_ot0)^zeta. This is the strength of the P3 positive feedback, and is scanned in E6 rather than fitted.

name: L_0
description: Baseline RANKL expression (dimensionless).

name: lambda_S
description: Maximum fold up-regulation of RANKL by sclerostin. Direction and order of magnitude follow the reported approximately 7-fold increase in osteoclastic activity.

name: K_L
description: Half-saturation constant for RANKL up-regulation by sclerostin.

name: lambda_P
description: Maximum fold up-regulation of RANKL by PTH. RECALIBRATED AT v2.14 (P5k). This parameter now sits at the centre of a genuine conflict the old decoupled module could not show: raising it helps V7 (calcium suppresses PTH, which protects bone) and hurts V16 (the post-withdrawal calcium flood suppresses PTH, which damps the resorption overshoot). No value satisfies both - V7 needs about 7 or more, V16 about 4 or less. 6 is the balanced choice, leaving both just outside their bands and well inside their declared tolerances. See appendix C27.

name: K_PL
description: Half-saturation constant for RANKL up-regulation by PTH.

name: lambda_E
description: Coefficient of direct oestrogen inhibition of RANKL. Risks compensating with lambda_T, so the two must not be freed for fitting simultaneously.

name: O_0
description: Baseline OPG expression (dimensionless).

name: lambda_beta
description: Maximum fold up-regulation of OPG by beta-catenin.

name: K_beta
description: Half-saturation constant for OPG up-regulation by beta-catenin.

name: W_0
description: Baseline Wnt signalling strength (dimensionless).

name: K_W
description: Half-saturation constant for sclerostin inhibition of Wnt.

name: m_W
description: Hill coefficient for sclerostin inhibition of Wnt.

name: k_beta
description: beta-catenin production rate.

name: delta_beta
description: beta-catenin degradation rate.

name: D_R
description: Differentiation timescale of osteoblast precursors (= D_OBu, Pivonka Table 3). VERIFIED AT v2.15: Lemaire 2004 Appendix A.3 gives D_R = 7e-4 pM/day, in agreement.

name: D_B
description: Differentiation timescale of osteoblasts (= D_OBp, Pivonka Table 3). Corrected at v1.9 from 7e-4, a factor of about 7600 - responding osteoblasts differentiate very fast. DO NOT 'correct' this to Lemaire's value: Lemaire gives D_B = f0*d_B = 0.035, but Pivonka 2008 rewrites the model with a different non-dimensionalisation and an explicit TGF-beta term, so the rate constants do not correspond term by term. See data/reference_parameters.md.

name: D_C
description: Differentiation timescale of osteoclast precursors (= D_OCp, Pivonka Table 3). Corrected at v1.9 from 2.1e-3, a factor of 100. DO NOT 'correct' this back to Lemaire's 2.1e-3: that is the same parameterisation difference as D_B. See data/reference_parameters.md.

name: D_A
description: Osteoclast apoptosis rate caused by TGF-beta (= A_OCa, Pivonka Table 3; D_A in Lemaire Appendix A.3). Literature value verified at v2.15 against the Lemaire 2004 full text: both papers give 0.7/day. NOT READ BY ANY CODE - M6 was rewritten in baseline-relative form, where the absolute apoptosis rate is absorbed into the D_C timescale; the name survives only in comments. Kept as provenance.

name: k_B
description: Rate of elimination of active osteoblasts (= A_OBa, Pivonka Table 3; k_B in Lemaire Appendix A.3). Literature value verified at v2.15 against the Lemaire 2004 full text: both papers give 0.189/day. NOT READ BY ANY CODE - see D_A; M6's baseline-relative form absorbs it into D_B. Kept as provenance.

name: K_L3
description: Half-saturation constant of RANKL for osteoclast differentiation, in the lumped Hill form pi_L = L/(K_L3 + L + kappa_OPG*O). NARROWED AT v2.15 from the held Pivonka 2008 and Lemaire 2004 full texts, but NOT fully resolved. Both papers use explicit competitive binding, whose occupancy is L/(1/K_A2 + L + (K_A1/K_A2)*O) with K_A2 = 3.412e-2 /pM (RANKL-RANK) and K_A1 = 1.0e-3 /pM (RANKL-OPG); Lemaire's k3/k4 and k1/k2 give the same two constants, so the sources agree. In pM this fixes 1/K_A2 = 29.31 pM. Our L and O are baseline-normalised, so the conversion is K_L3 = 1/(K_A2*L_0), and neither table reports the baseline RANKL concentration L_0 in compatible units. ONE UNKNOWN REMAINS, not a missing lookup.

name: kappa_OPG
description: Competitive inhibition coefficient of OPG against RANKL. NARROWED AT v2.15 alongside K_L3, same derivation: kappa_OPG = K_L3 * K_A1 * O_0, so the RATIO kappa_OPG/K_L3 = K_A1*O_0 is what the literature constrains, with K_A1 = 1.0e-3 /pM. The incumbent pair (K_L3 = kappa_OPG = 1) therefore implies a baseline OPG of about 1000 pM, which is the concrete claim a future source should be checked against. ONE UNKNOWN REMAINS, not a missing lookup.

name: gamma_beta
description: Coefficient for beta-catenin promotion of osteoblast precursor proliferation.

name: gamma_surv
description: Coefficient for beta-catenin promotion of osteoblast survival.

name: C_s_TGF
description: TGF-beta activation coefficient (= K_D1,TGF-beta, Pivonka Table 3; C^s in Lemaire, who gives 5e-3). Changed at v1.9 from 5e-3 to 4.545e-3 to follow Pivonka's parameterisation, not as a correction.

name: R_0
description: Baseline concentration of responding osteoblasts [pM]. CORRECTED AT v2.15 from 7.0e-4, which was a transcription slip: 7e-4 is the value of D_R on the adjacent row of the same table, while Lemaire's steady-state R is 7.734e-4. PROVENANCE ONLY - not read by any code: M6 works in baseline-relative units (R, B, C are 1 at baseline), so the absolute concentration is never needed. Verified against the Lemaire 2004 full text at v2.15 (Reference/10.pdf, transcribed in data/reference_parameters.md).

name: B_0
description: Baseline concentration of active osteoblasts [pM]. Exact Lemaire value; the table previously carried the rounded 7.3e-4. PROVENANCE ONLY - not read by any code: M6 works in baseline-relative units (R, B, C are 1 at baseline), so the absolute concentration is never needed. Verified against the Lemaire 2004 full text at v2.15 (Reference/10.pdf, transcribed in data/reference_parameters.md).

name: C_0
description: Baseline concentration of active osteoclasts [pM]. Exact Lemaire value; the table previously carried the rounded 9.1e-4. PROVENANCE ONLY - not read by any code: M6 works in baseline-relative units (R, B, C are 1 at baseline), so the absolute concentration is never needed. Verified against the Lemaire 2004 full text at v2.15 (Reference/10.pdf, transcribed in data/reference_parameters.md).

name: k_form
description: Surface deposition rate per unit osteoblast. DERIVED by balanceBoneFormation(p) from adult bone-mass balance, d(A_g*f_bm)/dt = 0, so it moves with k_res and is not a free parameter. WARNING: getDefaultParams reads this value from the table rather than re-deriving it, so it must be rewritten by hand whenever k_res or anything else in the balance changes. Recomputed at v2.14 (P5k) after the k_res recalibration; test_calibration/testFormationIsBoneMassBalanced is what catches a stale value.

name: k_res
description: Surface resorption rate per unit osteoclast. RECALIBRATED AT v2.14 (P5k) after the systemic calcium module was rebuilt; sets V1 turnover to 7.03 %/yr.

name: S_v_max
description: Peak of the specific-surface function (non-dimensionalised). Placeholder form: S_v = S_v_max * C * f^s1 * (1-f)^s2, pending replacement by the fifth-order polynomial of Martin 1984. LEREBOURS 2015 READ AT v2.19 (Reference/a06a.pdf) AND OUR EXPONENT IS WRONG FOR CORTEX. They state that at high bone volume fraction the relationship behaves as BS/TV = a*(1 - BV/TV)^b, with b = 1 for both the Martin fifth-order polynomial and the Fyhrie harmonic mean, and b = 0.5 for the square-root fit they propose and measure (r^2 = 0.84 against 0.82 and 0.77). Above BV/TV = 0.9 their data converge to zero at BV/TV = 1 with a fractional degree closer to a square root than to any integer polynomial. OUR s2_Sv IS 3, i.e. six times the measured exponent and three times even the polynomial alternative, and our cortical compartment sits at f_bm = 0.95 - squarely in the regime they measured. Consequence: d ln S_v / d ln f_bm is about -56 here where Lerebours implies about -9.5, so our specific surface responds roughly six-fold too steeply to porosity change. Baseline turnover is unaffected because S_v is normalised at baseline, but every RATE of change through S_v is exaggerated, V11's loss-recovery asymmetry included, since the source comments attribute that asymmetry to this very function. This is the same pathology as kappa_E before P5m: one functional form chosen in the trabecular regime (dome peaking at f_bm = 0.25) and then applied at f_bm = 0.95. Deferred to P5n; see appendix C30.

name: s1_Sv
description: First exponent of the specific-surface function. With the v2.19 cortical s2 of 0.5 the dome peaks at f_bm = s1/(s1+s2) = 0.67 in cortex, which is not a claim about where trabecular specific surface peaks - the trabecular compartment keeps s2 = 3 and its peak at 0.25. See s2_Sv.

name: s2_Sv
description: Second exponent of the specific-surface function, S_v proportional to f^s1 (1-f)^s2. P5n (v2.19) TRIED the measured cortical value of 0.5 and did NOT adopt it; the reason is the result. Lerebours 2015 measure b = 0.5 at high bone volume fraction (r^2 0.84, against 0.82 for Martin's fifth-order polynomial and 0.77 for the Fyhrie harmonic mean, both implying b = 1), and our cortex sits at f_bm = 0.95, squarely in that regime - so 3 is about six times the measured exponent. Setting it to 0.5 works mechanically: d ln S_v/d ln f_bm at the cortical baseline goes from -56 to -8.51, close to the -9.5 Lerebours implies. But it makes V2 UNREACHABLE. Disuse loss falls to 0.434 %/month, and scanning K_S to the bottom of its range saturates at 0.944 %/month, never entering the 1.0-1.5 band. That is a finding, not a tuning failure: the model's disuse loss was riding on an exaggerated specific-surface response, and with the measured exponent some other mechanism has to supply it. Shipped at 3 so the repository stays in a verified state; adopting 0.5 needs a recalibration that finds the missing disuse mechanism rather than pinning K_S at a bound. See appendix C30.

name: w_wall
description: Effective cortical wall thickness scale, used to convert surface rates into a rate of change of f_bm.

name: eps_model_star
description: Minimum effective strain threshold for periosteal modelling (Frost's MES_m, approximately 1000-1500 microstrain). Below it - and normal activity sits at 762 microstrain - there is no modelling, so the calibration scenarios are unaffected; above it, vigorous loading drives periosteal expansion. Added at v2.3 to separate Frost modelling from remodelling.

name: k_model
description: Periosteal modelling deposition rate per unit strain excess. Added at v2.3: it drives periosteal expansion directly from strain, produces the Haapasalo geometric gains (V6a-e), and is self-limiting (r_p up raises the second moment of area, which lowers strain). V6 is a hold-out, so this value is set on physical grounds and not fitted.

name: eps_model_sat
description: Half-saturation strain excess for periosteal modelling (added at v2.6). modeling = k_model*excess/(1 + excess/eps_sat), with excess = max(0, eps_p - eps_model_star). Two independent arguments converge on the same value: (1) at half-saturation the total strain is eps_model_star + eps_sat = 1500 + 5500 = 7000 microstrain, the yield strain of cortical bone, beyond which tissue enters damage rather than adaptation and Frost's linear relation cannot be extrapolated; (2) the implied rate ceiling v_max = k_model*eps_sat = 1.93 micrometres/day falls within the documented mineral apposition rate for rapid modelling and woven bone (approximately 1-5 micrometres/day). This correction removes the runaway periosteal artefact, which in the pathological state had demanded 1513 mm/yr.

name: chi_drift
description: Fraction of periosteal modelling deposition accompanied by endocortical resorption (added at v2.11). dr_e is incremented by chi_drift*modeling. Frost's modelling drift translates the cortex outward rather than merely inflating it; chi_drift = 1 is pure translation, preserving cortical wall thickness, while 0 recovers the v2.10 behaviour of adding without translating. The value 1.0 is a choice of principle (pure translation), NOT a fit to V6e - which is why V6e remains a hold-out. The term rides on modelling, so it inherits both that term's strain threshold (never triggered in any calibration scenario) and its saturation bound.

name: m_prim
description: Fraction of mineralisation achieved immediately as primary mineralisation.

name: kappa_m
description: Secondary (maturation) mineralisation rate. Added at v2.3 as the maturation term of the intensive rho_min ODE; the half-time of about 3.8 years matches the multi-year timescale of secondary mineralisation. Being slow, it prevents maturation from masking the post-withdrawal density loss V10.

name: mu_turn_0
description: Baseline mineralisation turnover rate, by which newly formed bone dilutes rho_min. Added at v2.3 so that rho_min falls as formation rises (new bone is less mineralised), which is what produces V6f. Its magnitude corresponds to the V1 turnover of about 7%/yr.

name: xi_p_0
description: Baseline allocation of resorption to the periosteal surface (adult periosteal resorption is minimal).

name: xi_e_0
description: Baseline allocation of resorption to the endocortical surface.

name: xi_i_0
description: Baseline allocation of resorption to the intracortical surface.

name: lambda_xi
description: Coefficient by which TNF-alpha biases resorption towards the endocortical surface. Determines the postmenopausal geometric phenotype V15.

name: a_p_abs
description: Paracellular fraction of intake absorbed, unsaturating and unregulated. REDUCED FROM 0.15 AT v2.14 (P5k): the paracellular route must not dominate, because it is the transcellular route that carries the calcitriol and PTH regulation which buffers dietary calcium. At the previous value the passive term supplied over 99.9 % of absorption and the regulated arm was inert.

name: a_a_abs
description: Maximum ACTIVE (transcellular) calcium absorption, expressed as a fraction of BASELINE intake so the parameter stays dimensionless while the flux it produces is mg/day: A_act = a_a_abs * I_Ca_0 = 280 mg/day. UNITS CORRECTED AT v2.14 (P5k): the v1.8 code used a_a_abs * I/(K_I+I) directly as though it were a flux, which made it a fraction of order 0.1 mg/day against a paracellular flux of 120 mg/day - the regulated arm of absorption was therefore absent, which is why serum calcium swung 15 % with intake.

name: K_I_abs
description: Half-saturation constant of active absorption with respect to intake. The key parameter behind the plateau shape of V7, and from v2.14 also the reason fractional absorption falls as intake rises (29 % at 400 mg/day, 22 % at 1500 mg/day).

name: K_VD
description: Half-saturation constant for 1,25D promotion of active absorption. RESOLVED AT v2.15 from the Peterson & Riggs 2010 full text already held: their Table 1 sets the calcitriol-dependent calcium absorption state to 0.5 (unitless) at baseline, and our absorption gate is V_D/(K_VD + V_D) with V_D_0 = 1, which equals 0.5 exactly when K_VD = 1. The incumbent value is therefore confirmed rather than assumed. No longer awaiting literature.

name: phi_res
description: Skeletal calcium released to the serum pool per unit baseline-relative resorption [mg/day]. RAISED FROM 0.10 AT v2.14 (P5k). The old value came from comparing the skeletal calcium POOL with daily turnover and concluding the coefficient must be far below 1; the quantity that belongs here is the ratio of skeletal calcium FLUX to daily flux, and those are the same order. At 0.10 against a normalising absorption of ~120 mg/day, bone could not move serum calcium at all: 180 days of unloading moved PTH by 0.01 % where bed-rest subjects show 17-24 % suppression (Spatz 2012, PMID 22767636). 350 mg/day is the order of adult skeletal calcium turnover.

name: phi_form
description: Skeletal calcium removed from the serum pool per unit baseline-relative formation [mg/day]. Equal to phi_res so the exchange vanishes at baseline and carries the true flux under perturbation. See phi_res for why v2.14 raised both.

name: P_max
description: Maximum PTH secretion rate. NOT AWAITING LITERATURE and not read by any code: the PTH set point is normalised so that Pset = 1 at baseline (Pset = gP(Ca_s)/gP(Ca_s_0)), which makes any overall secretion scale a gauge with no observable consequence. Corrected at v2.15, where the old note 'Awaits Peterson & Riggs 2010' was found to be asking for a number that cannot matter.

name: Ca_50
description: Serum calcium concentration at half-maximal inhibition of PTH secretion (ionised calcium).

name: n_P
description: Hill coefficient of PTH secretion with respect to serum calcium. RAISED FROM 4 AT v2.14 (P5k), and it is a shape constraint rather than a fit: the classic PTH-calcium sigmoid runs from near-maximal to near-minimal secretion over roughly 1.0-1.4 mmol/L ionised calcium, a better than tenfold range over +/-17 %, which is a logarithmic slope near the set point of about -8. Since that slope is n_P/2 at the midpoint, n_P is about 16. At the old value of 4 the slope was -2, and reproducing the 20 % PTH suppression of immobilisation would have required a 10 % rise in serum calcium, i.e. frank hypercalcaemia.

name: delta_P
description: PTH clearance rate (= k_7D, 7.143/h = 171/day, half-life 5.8 min, Peterson-Riggs Table 2). Corrected at v1.9 from 48.

name: k_VD
description: 1,25D production rate. NOT AWAITING LITERATURE and not read by any code: VDset is normalised to 1 at baseline and the approach rate is carried by delta_VD, so this scale is a gauge. Corrected at v2.15; see P_max.

name: K_VP
description: Half-saturation constant for PTH promotion of 1,25D production.

name: delta_VD
description: 1,25D clearance rate (half-life of several hours to a day).

name: Ca_s_0
description: Baseline serum ionised calcium.

name: renal_k
description: Gain of renal calcium excretion above the tubular threshold [mg/day per mmol/L]. DERIVED, not free: renal_k = (Abs_0 + phi_res - phi_form)/(Ca_s_0 - renal_Ca_th) closes the baseline balance, so the steepness of the renal defence is set entirely by where the threshold sits. IMPLEMENTED AT v2.14 (P5k) - declared since v1.8 but never read by any code, which is why excretion was a bare power law in Ca_s.

name: renal_Ca_th
description: Renal tubular threshold for calcium [mmol/L]: excretion is the excess of serum calcium over this, and it is the single free physiological choice governing how tightly serum calcium is defended. Placing it about 2 % below Ca_s_0 makes excretion a small difference of two large numbers and therefore steeply sensitive - the same statement as 'about 98 % of filtered calcium is reabsorbed'. IMPLEMENTED AT v2.14 (P5k); previously declared but unused.

name: renal_lambda_P
description: PTH shift of the tubular threshold, as a fraction of the (Ca_s_0 - renal_Ca_th) gap: Ca_th = renal_Ca_th + renal_lambda_P * gap * (P - 1). Higher PTH raises the threshold, so less calcium is excreted. SCALED BY THE GAP, NOT BY Ca_th (v2.14): the gap is only ~2 % of Ca_th, so shifting the threshold by a percentage of its own value would swamp the entire defence with a few percent of PTH movement.

name: kappa_Ca
description: Relaxation rate of the serum calcium pool [1/day]. Serum calcium is held constant by the calcium-sensing receptor and PTH on a timescale of minutes, far faster than bone remodelling (days to months). From v2.14 the flux imbalance is divided by renal_k, so this is directly the relaxation rate rather than a rate times a flux ratio.

name: n_renal
description: [Retired at v2.14] Hill steepness of the old renal power law Renal_0*(Ca_s/Ca_s_0)^n_renal. Superseded by the threshold form built on renal_k and renal_Ca_th. Retained for comparison only. Its docstring claimed this mechanism held serum calcium within about 2 %; measured, it held it within 15 % (appendix C24.5).

name: I_Ca_0
description: Baseline dietary calcium intake (the centre of the low- and high-calcium arms of experiment E2).

name: V_D_0
description: Baseline 1,25D (defined by non-dimensionalisation).

name: E2_0
description: Baseline oestrogen (defined as 1 premenopausally by non-dimensionalisation; postmenopausal scenarios set it to 0.1).
